![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14253507/assets/e24e093814eeaaf82b1c7e2d5c60648407f9f5aaf717de1138f08505b579651e.png)

Which of the following gives the area bounded between the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=2{e}^{-t},\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡t
$$

and the $x$-axis for $t\in [0,\pi ]?$
question.worked_solution:
The unsigned area bounded by the parametric curve 

$$
x=x(t),\,y=y(t),\,{t}_{1}\le t\le {t}_{2}
$$

and the $x$-axis is given by the absolute value of the integral

$$
{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{-t}) \\  & =-2{e}^{-t}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain the integral expression

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }3\operatorname{sin}⁡t(-2{e}^{-t})\,\text{d}t \\  & =-6{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that this integral will give us a negative number since $y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\le 0$ for all $t\in [0,\pi ].$

Therefore, the area is given by

$$
A=-(-6{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t)=6{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t.
$$
